additional_info.subject: RE: ID0413048-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / N9 160381805] EVSE_TEMPUpperLimit CRM:00921001633
additional_info.body:
Hello Team,
The device has a "PT1000_BT5_AC-Income" error.
Please plan a site intervention to check the following points:
Check for Loose Connections:
Inspect the BT5 circuit thoroughly to ensure that there are no loose connections. Pay special attention to all connectors and wiring around the circuit.
BT5 Sensor Measurement:
Check all the BT5 sensors, as the values of some may be outside the permissible limits.
Measure the resistance of each sensor and verify whether it aligns with the temperature values as per the PT1000 chart (attached).
If the resistance values are not within the normal range, replace the sensor.
Measurement at XD34:17 & XD34:18:
Measure the resistance between XD34:17 and XD34:18. The expected value should be approximately 1050 ohms.
If this value is present, the BT5 sensor is functioning correctly.
Measure Resistance at KF6 (M3+ and M3-):
Measure the resistance between M3+ and M3- at the KF6 connector.
A resistance value greater than 250kΩ indicates a problem, and the circuit is not in good condition.
Measurement at XD9.2B:
Measure the resistance between pins 1 & 2 at the XD9.2B connector.
A resistance reading of approximately 1050 ohms indicates that the circuit is functioning properly.
Open Circuit Test at XD9.2B:
Disconnect the XD9.2B connector and measure the resistance between pins 1 & 2.
The result should show infinite resistance, indicating that the circuit is open, which is a good sign.
After reconnecting the XD9.2B connector, verify whether the BT5 error flags have been cleared.
Check XD9.2A Connection:
Ensure that the XD9.2A connector is properly connected.
Note that this might be more challenging, as the connector is located inside the unit.
KF6 Pin Check:
Power down the charger completely and remove the KF6 connector.
Inspect the pins for any visible damage or wear.
Reconnect the KF6 connector, ensuring there are no gaps between the pins and that the connection is secure.
MLFB No:
8EM5903-0AA00-1AA3 – BT3, BT4, BT5 Temperature Sensor PT1000
M8
5m
.
Additional Notes:
A photo of a similar issue from another charger is attached for your reference, which may help in diagnosing the current issue
.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team - Ankita
